explanation: Processor pipelining is a technique that improves instruction execution speed by overlapping the execution of multiple instructions.  Instead of completing one instruction before starting the next, different stages of instruction execution (fetch, decode, execute, memory access, write back) are performed concurrently on different instructions.  However, this concurrency can lead to hazards (data, control, or structural) that require handling to ensure correct execution.  Understanding and mitigating these hazards is crucial for optimizing processor performance.
